name: Mab

attributes.attribute: a fairy queen in Welsh folklore who appears as the fairies' midwife in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet
the Irish great goddess, diminished over time into a quasi-historical queen

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mab was a fairy queen in Welsh folklore. She offers only a hint of earlier divinity. Ireland turned the great goddess Medb into a quasi-historical queen over time. Wales worked the same change on this figure. Queen Mab appears in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet as the fairies' midwife, a role once played by a human victim of fairy kidnapping. Shakespeare also gave Mab the duty to bring nightmares. Scholars link her playful name to the Welsh word mab, which means child. The same word appears in the collection of myths called the Mabinogion. Shakespeare borrowed British and Welsh fairy lore at will. His portraits of mythological beings are vivid but not always accurate.

okr.objective: Document Mab as a Welsh fairy queen who descends from the goddess Medb.
